key_insight: The paper proposes a restricted quantum-computing interface, 1/2BQP_1, where random hidden basis inputs and a single output bit aim to preserve useful quantum computation while preventing efficient RSA factoring by untrusted users.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for designing public quantum cloud services that can safely expose fault-tolerant hardware without giving users full cryptanalytic leverage.
method: Define a restricted computation model with random computational-basis inputs revealed only after execution and one designated output bit.
Argue that standard factoring quantum subroutines become classically simulable under one-bit readout, covering Shor-like and related constructions.
Analyze a potential attack via coherent rational reconstruction and argue it is blocked by random inputs and believed circuit lower bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a two-step theoretical security argument, including classical simulability results for broad factoring constructions and a hardness claim tied to rational reconstruction parallelization limits.
watch_item: Security depends on unproven complexity assumptions, especially conjectured lower bounds for rational reconstruction and the hardness of factoring in this restricted setting.
paper_title: Protecting Quantum Computers against Untrusted Users
